_about: One record per option for safer, more convenient trips: the toolkit-matrix block's scorecard. Each figure is read from the option's What We Know research, with its provenance tag. A null figure is not measured: never estimated to fill the row. Site copy: site/data/options/scorecard.json, by tools/toolkit/build-scorecard-site.py. Fields: grade (the Maryland scale level or why there is none), search (a search the limit cut short), studies (rows in data/evidence/studies.json), method (the methods row). cost.tied_to_miles means the low miles go with the low cost, because more money buys more miles. vmt_reduction.rank_on_central ranks and charts a row on its central figure alone. short is the chart label.

_cost_basis.text: Cost a year: running cost plus build cost spread over 10 years. One basis for every option, used for the chart's x axis and the Top asks ranking. The 12-month cell trial and the one-off e-bike pilot (spread_years 1) count their whole cost in that year.

_mode_shift_base.text: Counts of people who stop being driven become citywide car share points at two trips each a school day or workday, against 4.46 million daily person trips to, from and within SF. The note doesn't say whether that is a weekday or a seven-day average, and school-day trips run about 180 days a year, so the points are an upper bound.

_dropped.downtown-congestion-pricing: Merged into road-pricing: the 2026-11-05 road pricing note covers the same $6.50 cordon and supersedes it.
_dropped.connected-bike-network-comfort-standard: Merged into protected-bike-network: same method (D1). Its comfort standard is how that network gets built. Its own 1.7M to 47.7M miles, at about $15M a year, rest on an assumed share of riders from cars and are in that row's note.

_intro: Our estimates, not measurements, researched October 31 to November 6, 2026.

_view_notes.mode: An upper limit, counting two trips a school day or workday per person, out of daily trips to, from and within SF.
_view_notes.injury: Each change counts different injuries: everyone hurt, only deaths and severe injuries, or only children. Citywide changes are spread over SF's 47 square miles.

_sources_note: “No estimate” means we have none, and we don't guess one. Study grades (Maryland scale) run 1 (weakest) to 5 (randomized) and rate the study, not its fit to SF. Existing money says whether a budget or grant's own rule covers the change.

options.name: Corridor and mobile speed cameras
options.way: Move beyond SF's 33 single fixed camera spots to corridor and mobile cameras on the High Injury Network (WWK: 'For SF, the research points to moving beyond single spots'; recommendation 'Allow corridor and mobile cameras'). The newest notes make this concrete as a state-law change: a signed list of HIN sites, up to thousands, with mobile cameras assigned at random each day, Queensland-style, each counting once against a raised cap.

injuries_avoided_per_year.whose: not estimated for the corridor/mobile scope

status.plan: No adopted or draft City plan for corridor or mobile cameras. Board Resolution 408-26 (File 260499, 10-1, 2026-07-14) only 'supports exploring changes to State law ... including increasing the number of allowable speed camera locations, with priority given to corridors on the High Injury Network'; SFMTA 'expects to advocate for expansion of the program to incrementally increase the number of camera locations' (18-month report, p. 4). State law already allows mobile units from about March 2027 (§22426(f)) but caps SF at 33 systems.

readiness.sf_record: SF's first camera went live 2025-03-20 and all 33 locations pass the AB 645 18-month test (10+ mph-over speeding down 84%); the Board adopted Resolution 408-26 supporting more locations 10-1 on 2026-07-14 (Walton no) and the Mayor returned it unsigned; SB 1279 (2026) added two Long Beach cameras while the Assembly Transportation Committee said the Legislature 'should wait for data'; any site move needs community review and an SFMTA Board vote.
opposed_by: Peace Officers Research Association of California (PORAC)
Supervisor Walton (lone no vote on Resolution 408-26)
Cal Walks (named in the WWK as an equity critic)
